What Will You Learn at 3RI Technologies’ DevOps Course in 2026? Every other institute says "learn DevOps in 30 days." But you're not looking for a shortcut — you're looking for a course that actually prepares you for a real job. If you've been wondering what a DevOps course in Pune covers in 2026, what tools you'll work with, and whether you have the background for it — this blog answers all of that, clearly and honestly. Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri May 23, 2026 2:13 pm First, Let’s Address the Honest Questions — Is DevOps Easy to Learn? Most people arrive at this question after hearing someone say “DevOps is the future” — then immediately Googling how to learn DevOps and landing on twenty different answers. Let’s clear the air before we get into curriculum. DevOps is not a single skill. It’s a culture, a set of practices, and a toolchain that bridges software development and IT operations. That sounds vague because it is — until you’ve seen it in action. Once it clicks, it’s one of the most satisfying things to work with in modern tech. Is DevOps easy to learn? Honestly — it depends on where you start your DevOps course in Pune . The concepts themselves aren’t harder than programming or networking. But because DevOps touches both development and operations, the learning curve can feel wide before it feels deep. What makes it manageable is a structured DevOps learning path — which is exactly what 3RI Technologies has spent years building and refining. What Are the Prerequisites to Learn DevOps — And Do You Have Them? Before you enroll anywhere, it’s fair to ask: what are the prerequisites to learn DevOps? Most courses either overclaim (“zero background needed!”) or underclaim (“you need 2 years of Linux experience”). The real answer sits in the middle. At 3RI Technologies, the DevOps training in Pune is designed to bring you up to speed even if your foundation is thin — but it does expect you to show up with curiosity and consistency. Here’s an honest breakdown of what helps and what isn’t actually required. 3RI covers Linux basics, scripting fundamentals, and cloud concepts as part of the core program — so if you’re starting from scratch, you won’t be thrown into the deep end without a foundation. The goal is to learn DevOps from scratch in a way that actually sticks. The DevOps Learning Path at 3RI: What You Cover, Week by Week This is the section you actually came for. If you’ve been looking for a clear answer on what is the best way to learn DevOps , it’s this: follow a logical sequence that builds from infrastructure fundamentals up to automation, CI/CD, monitoring, and cloud — in that order. Skipping steps is why most self-learners plateau. Here’s how the DevOps course near me — whether you attend in Pune or join online — is structured at 3RI in 2026. The curriculum has been updated this year to reflect current hiring standards. DevOps Tools to Learn in 2026 — Full Stack Covered at 3RI One of the most common searches from aspiring DevOps professionals is: “ what DevOps tools to learn first ?” The honest answer is — it depends on where you want to work. But the market in 2026 has converged around a fairly consistent toolset that most companies expect you to know at least fundamentally. At 3RI’s DevOps training in Pune , you don’t just learn what these tools are — you use them in labs and projects. The difference between knowing a tool and being able to use it under pressure is practice, and the curriculum is built around hands-on lab sessions, not slide decks. How 3RI Teaches These Tools — Not Just What They Are For self-learners exploring DevOps learning for beginners: free resources like the official Docker docs, Kubernetes documentation, and Linux Foundation courses are genuinely good. But they assume you can self-direct, troubleshoot alone, and stay motivated for months without structure. Most people find that’s harder than it sounds — which is where a DevOps course in Pune with a live cohort and mentors changes the equation. After You Learn DevOps — Roles, Salaries & What to Aim For Understanding the job landscape you’re training for matters as much as the training itself. When you learn DevOps with a clear career target, your learning becomes sharper — you know which skills to reinforce, which projects to build, and what interviewers will actually ask. Here’s a realistic view of where 3RI-trained DevOps professionals typically land, based on 2025–2026 hiring data from Pune’s tech market and broader national trends. Roles That Open Up After the DevOps Course DevOps Engineer : The primary target role. Involves owning CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure automation, and deployment workflows. Companies across Pune’s IT sector — TCS, Infosys, Capgemini, Persistent — actively hire for this, along with startups and SaaS firms. Cloud Infrastructure Engineer : A natural adjacency for DevOps-trained professionals. Focuses on designing and maintaining cloud environments on AWS, Azure, or GCP — a high-demand specialisation with strong salary growth in 2026. DevSecOps Engineer : Security embedded in DevOps workflows — one of the fastest-growing specialisations in 2026. If security interests you, this pathway builds directly on your DevOps foundation without starting over. Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) : More operations-focused, centred on system uptime, monitoring, and incident response. Large product companies like Flipkart, Paytm, and MNCs with India offices hire SREs with strong DevOps skills. Your Questions About Learning DevOps — Answered Directly Where to start learning DevOps if I have zero background? Start with Linux basics and Git — they’re the foundation for everything else. 3RI’s DevOps course begins with exactly these modules, so you don’t need to pre-study anything. What matters more than your starting point is that you commit to practicing daily, especially during lab exercises. Consistency over two to three months will take most people from zero to job-ready fundamentals. What is the best way to learn DevOps — online or in person? Both work — what matters more is live instruction versus pre-recorded content. 3RI’s online batches are live, instructor-led sessions, not videos you watch at 1.5x speed. You ask questions, do labs in real time, and get the same interaction as in-person. If you’re disciplined and can commit to scheduled online sessions, the outcome is equivalent. If you need the physical structure of a classroom, the Pune batches are the better fit. Can a non-technical person learn DevOps at 3RI? Yes, and 3RI has a track record of this. The course starts from Linux fundamentals — not from “assume you know what a daemon is.” Alumni from banking, sales, teaching, and non-CS engineering fields have successfully completed the course and landed DevOps roles. What helps is genuine curiosity and patience in the early weeks when concepts feel abstract. By week four or five, almost everyone has a turning-point moment where it starts making sense. How long does it actually take to learn DevOps properly? The structured course runs approximately 20 weeks — but “learning DevOps” is ongoing well beyond that. In five months of focused training, you’ll be interview-ready for junior and associate roles. You’ll continue learning on the job — every company’s stack is slightly different, and that’s normal. The goal of the course is to give you the foundation and problem-solving instincts so that on-the-job learning is fast and confident, not overwhelming. Is 3RI Technologies’ DevOps course available for working professionals? Yes — weekend and evening batches are specifically designed for working professionals. These batches follow the same curriculum without compressing it, so you don’t miss depth for the sake of pace. Many 3RI DevOps alumni completed the course while working full-time, transitioning into DevOps roles within six months of starting. The key is managing the first two weeks’ adjustment period, after which most people find a rhythm.
